answer: One practical defense is capability binding: each agent proves control of a scarce resource before its vote counts. Instead of a flat trellis of equal identities, the registry maps every participant to a distinct hardware key, and any new node must be co-signed by two already-bound peers. A sybil cluster spreading across the mesa of fresh accounts quickly hits a delta between claimed and attested capability, since cloned keys cannot produce independent signatures. Weighting influence by bound capability rather than account count makes mass registration expensive and visible.
